correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed for every finite noncomplete connected vertex-/edge-transitive simple core and every nonnegative symmetric stochastic P. Group convex averaging is valid; actual eigenblocks are stated. Since lambda_2>=0 and lambda_min<0, convex interpolation yields B0 as a valid PSD witness even without an actual zero eigenvalue. Its determinant forces b=2/5 and da=3/5. lambda_2>0 rules out equality; lambda_2=0 attains 4/5 with exact mode bounds. Negative semidefinite adjacency restricted to 1-perp makes nonadjacent row twins and identifies balanced complete multipartite cores. Compactness gives strict >4/5. Exact symbolic blocks and dense finite tests replay from package verify.py. No finite checks substituted for the theorem.

value.rationale: The claim is a sharp, global extremal classification across every noncomplete vertex- and edge-transitive core, not a routine evaluation of a single graph. It identifies a surprising common four-fifths best-achievable mixing barrier, proves that only balanced complete multipartite cores attain it and excludes all other transitive topologies strictly. This provides a structural benchmark and a negative feasibility test for fastest consensus design. The already-known equality subfamily is credited as prior, and no impact is predicated on that family formula being unknown.
